text: Among $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{S},\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O},\mathrm{NF}_{3},\mathrm{NH}_{3}$ and $\mathrm{CHCl}_{3}$, identify the molecule $(\mathrm{X})$ with lowest dipole moment value. The number of lone pairs of electrons present on the central atom of the molecule $(X)$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 22nd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{ll} \text{Molecule} & \text{Dipole moment} \\ \mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{S} & 0.95 \\ \mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O} & 1.85 \\ \mathrm{NF}_{3} & 0.23\text{(minimum)} \\ \mathrm{NH}_{3} & 1.47 \\ \mathrm{CHCl}_{3} & 1.04 \end{array}$

From the given values, the dipole moment is the smallest for $\mathrm{NF}_{3}$ (it is $0.23$), so molecule $(X)$ is $\mathrm{NF}_{3}$.

In $\mathrm{NF}_{3}$, the central atom is nitrogen $(\mathrm{N})$.

Nitrogen has $5$ valence electrons. It makes $3$ $\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{F}$ bonds, so $3$ electrons are used for bonding.

The remaining $2$ valence electrons stay on nitrogen as one lone pair.

So, the number of lone pairs on the central atom in $(X)=\mathrm{NF}_{3}$ is $1$.


[IMG]


Number of lone pair on central atom = 1

text:
Given below are two statements :

Statement I : $\mathrm{C}<\mathrm{O}<\mathrm{N}<\mathrm{F}$ is the correct order in terms of first ionization enthalpy values.

Statement II : $\mathrm{S}>\mathrm{Se}>\mathrm{Te}>\mathrm{Po}>\mathrm{O}$ is the correct order in terms of the magnitude of electron gain enthalpy values.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 22nd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Statement I (First ionization enthalpy)
Across a period, first ionization enthalpy generally increases due to increasing nuclear charge and decreasing atomic size.

But there is an important NCERT exception:

Nitrogen ($\mathrm{N}$) has a half-filled configuration $2p^{3}$, which is extra stable.

Oxygen ($\mathrm{O}$) has configuration $2p^{4}$, where one $p$-orbital contains a pair of electrons, causing extra electron–electron repulsion, so it is easier to remove one electron.

So,

$\mathrm{IE}_{1}(\mathrm{O})<\mathrm{IE}_{1}(\mathrm{N})$

Also, in general:

$\mathrm{C}<\mathrm{O}<\mathrm{N}<\mathrm{F}$

✅ Statement I is true.

Statement II (Magnitude of electron gain enthalpy)
Electron gain enthalpy usually becomes less negative down a group due to increasing size (incoming electron feels less attraction).

But for group 16, NCERT notes:

Oxygen is very small, so the incoming electron experiences strong repulsion in the compact $2p$ subshell.

Hence oxygen has less negative electron gain enthalpy than sulphur.

Sulphur has the most negative (highest magnitude) electron gain enthalpy in this group.

Therefore, the magnitude order is:

$\mathrm{S}>\mathrm{Se}>\mathrm{Te}>\mathrm{Po}>\mathrm{O}$

✅ Statement II is true.

Correct option: D
✅ Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 22nd January Evening Shift

text:
Consider the following reduction processes :

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{Al}^{3+}+3\mathrm{e}^{-}⟶\mathrm{Al}(\mathrm{s}),\mathrm{E}^{0}=-1.66\mathrm{V} \\ \mathrm{Fe}^{3+}+\mathrm{e}^{-}⟶\mathrm{Fe}^{2+},\mathrm{E}^{0}=+0.77\mathrm{V} \\ \mathrm{Co}^{3+}+\mathrm{e}^{-}⟶\mathrm{Co}^{2+},\mathrm{E}^{0}=+1.81\mathrm{V} \\ \mathrm{Cr}^{3+}+3\mathrm{e}^{-}⟶\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{s}),\mathrm{E}^{0}=-0.74\mathrm{V} \end{array}$

The tendency to act as reducing agent decreases in the order :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 22nd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Reducing agent is the species that gets oxidised (donates electrons). In NCERT terms:

More negative $E_{\text{red}}^{\circ }$ for a couple $\Rightarrow$ the reduced form is a stronger reducing agent (it will be more easily oxidised).

Equivalently, higher $E_{\text{ox}}^{\circ }$ $\Rightarrow$ stronger reducing agent.

Now write oxidation potentials for the given reducing species:

1) From $\mathrm{Al}^{3+}+3e^{-}\to \mathrm{Al}(s),E_{\text{red}}^{\circ }=-1.66\text{V}$

$\mathrm{Al}(s)\to \mathrm{Al}^{3+}+3e^{-},E_{\text{ox}}^{\circ }=+1.66\text{V}$

2) From $\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}+3e^{-}\to \mathrm{Cr}(s),E_{\text{red}}^{\circ }=-0.74\text{V}$

$\mathrm{Cr}(s)\to \mathrm{Cr}^{3+}+3e^{-},E_{\text{ox}}^{\circ }=+0.74\text{V}$

3) From $\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}+e^{-}\to \mathrm{Fe}^{2+},E_{\text{red}}^{\circ }=+0.77\text{V}$

$\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}\to \mathrm{Fe}^{3+}+e^{-},E_{\text{ox}}^{\circ }=-0.77\text{V}$

4) From $\mathrm{Co}^{3+}+e^{-}\to \mathrm{Co}^{2+},E_{\text{red}}^{\circ }=+1.81\text{V}$

$\mathrm{Co}^{2+}\to \mathrm{Co}^{3+}+e^{-},E_{\text{ox}}^{\circ }=-1.81\text{V}$

Now arrange reducing strength (decreasing $E_{\text{ox}}^{\circ }$):

$+1.66>+0.74>-0.77>-1.81$

So, tendency to act as reducing agent decreases as:

$\mathrm{Al}>\mathrm{Cr}>\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}>\mathrm{Co}^{2+}$

Correct option: D
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 22nd January Evening Shift

text: The compound $\mathrm{A},\mathrm{C}_{8}\mathrm{H}_{8}\mathrm{O}_{2}$ reacts with acetophenone to form a single product via cross-Aldol condensation. The compound A on reaction with conc. NaOH forms a substituted benzyl alcohol as one of the two products. The compound A is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 22nd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{C}{}_{8}\mathrm{H}{}_{8}\mathrm{O}{}_{2}$ fits 4-methoxybenzaldehyde, $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{OC}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{4}\mathrm{CHO}$, as well as 2-hydroxyacetophenone and 4-methylbenzoic acid; 4-hydroxybenzaldehyde is $\mathrm{C}{}_{7}\mathrm{H}{}_{6}\mathrm{O}{}_{2}$.

4-Methoxybenzaldehyde has no $α$-H, so it cannot form an enolate and acts only as the acceptor towards the enolate of acetophenone; the crossed aldol (Claisen–Schmidt) condensation therefore gives a single product:

$\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{OC}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{4}\mathrm{CHO}+\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{COCH}{}_{3}{}_{\Delta }^{\mathrm{NaOH}\qquad }\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{OC}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{4}\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CHCOC}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}+\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$

The $β$-hydroxy ketone formed first loses water readily because the new $\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{C}$ is conjugated with both the ring and the $\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{O}$, so the product is the $α,β$-unsaturated ketone, one structure that can exist as geometrical isomers.

An aldehyde without $α$-H undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction with conc. NaOH, giving the substituted benzyl alcohol:

$2~\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{OC}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{4}\mathrm{CHO}{}^{\mathrm{conc}\cdot \mathrm{NaOH}}\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{OC}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{4}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{OH}+\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{OC}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{4}\mathrm{COONa}$

2-Hydroxyacetophenone has $α$-H and no aldehyde group, so it cannot undergo the Cannizzaro reaction, and 4-methylbenzoic acid undergoes neither reaction.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 22nd January Evening Shift

text:
Identify the correct statements :

A. Hydrated salts can be used as primary standard.

B. Primary standard should not undergo any reaction with air.

C. Reactions of primary standard with another substance should be instantaneous and stoichiometric.

D. Primary standard should not be soluble in water.

E. Primary standard should have low relative molar mass.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: A, B, C and E Only
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 22nd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Primary standard (as per NCERT idea) should be a substance which is pure, stable in air, non-hygroscopic, readily soluble in water, and reacts completely with the titrant in a stoichiometric way.

Now check each statement:

A. Hydrated salts can be used as primary standard.  

Some hydrated salts are sufficiently stable and can be used (example often cited: Mohr’s salt). So this can be correct.

B. Primary standard should not undergo any reaction with air.  

Correct. It should not react with $O_{2}$, $CO_{2}$ or moisture of air.

C. Reactions of primary standard with another substance should be instantaneous and stoichiometric.  

Correct. The reaction should be fast and have a definite stoichiometry so the end point is sharp.

D. Primary standard should not be soluble in water.  

Incorrect. It should be readily soluble so that a standard solution can be prepared.

E. Primary standard should have low relative molar mass.  

Incorrect. It should preferably have high molar mass to minimise weighing error.

So, correct statements are A, B and C only.

Correct option: Option D (A, B and C Only).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 22nd January Evening Shift

text:
Correct statements regarding Arrhenius equation among the following are :

A. Factor $e^{-\mathrm{Ea}/\mathrm{RT}}$ corresponds to fraction of molecules having kinetic energy less than Ea.

B. At a given temperature, lower the Ea, faster is the reaction.

C. Increase in temperature by about $10^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$ doubles the rate of reaction.

D. Plot of $\log \mathrm{k}$ vs $\frac{1}{\mathrm{T}}$ gives a straight line with slope $=-\frac{\mathrm{Ea}}{\mathrm{R}}$.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 22nd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Arrhenius equation (NCERT) is  

$k=Ae^{-E_{a}/RT}$  

and in base-10 logarithm form,  

$\log k=\log A-\frac{E_{a}}{2.303R}\left (\frac{1}{T}\right )$

Now check each statement:

A. $e^{-E_{a}/RT}$ corresponds to fraction of molecules having kinetic energy less than $E_{a}$.  

Incorrect. This factor represents the fraction of molecules having energy equal to or greater than $E_{a}$ (able to cross the energy barrier).

B. At a given temperature, lower the $E_{a}$, faster is the reaction.  

Correct. From $k=Ae^{-E_{a}/RT}$, smaller $E_{a}\Rightarrow$ larger $e^{-E_{a}/RT}\Rightarrow$ larger $k$.

C. Increase in temperature by about $10^{\circ }\text{C}$ doubles the rate of reaction.  

Correct as a common empirical rule mentioned in NCERT: for many reactions, rate approximately doubles for a $10^{\circ }\text{C}$ rise.

D. Plot of $\log k$ vs $\frac{1}{T}$ gives a straight line with slope $=-\frac{E_{a}}{R}$.  

Incorrect. For $\log$ (base 10), slope is  

$-\frac{E_{a}}{2.303R}$  

The slope $-\frac{E_{a}}{R}$ is for plotting $\ln k$ vs $\frac{1}{T}$.

So, correct statements are B and C only.

Correct option: Option C.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 22nd January Evening Shift

text:
$[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{PPh}_{3})_{2}\mathrm{Cl}_{2}]$ is a paramagnetic complex. Identify the INCORRECT statements about this complex.

A. The complex exhibits geometrical isomerism.

B. The complex is white in colour.

C. The calculated spin-only magnetic moment of the complex is 2.84 BM .

D. The calculated CFSE (Crystal Field Stabilization Energy) of Ni in this complex is $-0.8\Delta _{\mathrm{o}}$.

E. The geometrical arrangement of ligands in this complex is similar to that in $\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CO})_{4}$.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 22nd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For $[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{PPh}_{3})_{2}\mathrm{Cl}_{2}]$:

1) Oxidation state and $d$-electron count
$\mathrm{PPh}_{3}$ is neutral and each $\mathrm{Cl}$ is $-1$.

So oxidation state of Ni is $+2$.

$\mathrm{Ni}^{2+}\Rightarrow 3d^{8}$

2) Geometry using given information (paramagnetic)
For $\mathrm{Ni}^{2+}$ ($d^{8}$):

Square planar complexes are usually diamagnetic (all electrons paired).

Since the complex is paramagnetic, it must be tetrahedral (in NCERT level treatment).

So geometry is tetrahedral and it has 2 unpaired electrons.

Check each statement
A. The complex exhibits geometrical isomerism.
In a tetrahedral complex, all four positions are equivalent, so an $\mathrm{MA}_{2}\mathrm{B}_{2}$ type complex does not show cis–trans isomerism.

So A is incorrect.

B. The complex is white in colour.
Tetrahedral $\mathrm{Ni}^{2+}$ complexes are generally coloured due to $d$–$d$ transitions; “white” is not expected.

So B is incorrect.

C. Spin-only magnetic moment is $2.84\mathrm{BM}$.
Number of unpaired electrons $n=2$.

$μ_{\text{so}}=\sqrt{n(n+2)}=\sqrt{2(2+2)}=\sqrt{8}=2.83\mathrm{BM}\approx 2.84\mathrm{BM}$

So C is correct.

D. CFSE is $-0.8\Delta _{o}$.
For tetrahedral splitting, we must use $\Delta _{t}$, not $\Delta _{o}$.

For $d^{8}$ tetrahedral: $e^{4}t_{2}^{4}$

$\text{CFSE}=4(-0.6\Delta _{t})+4(+0.4\Delta _{t})=(-2.4+1.6)\Delta _{t}=-0.8\Delta _{t}$

So writing $-0.8\Delta _{o}$ is wrong.

So D is incorrect.

E. Geometry similar to $\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CO})_{4}$.
$\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CO})_{4}$ is tetrahedral, and this complex is also tetrahedral (as concluded from paramagnetism).

So E is correct.

Incorrect statements: A, B and D
✅ Correct option: Option B (A, B and D Only)
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 22nd January Evening Shift

text: The dibromo compound $[\mathrm{P}]$ (molecular formula: $\mathrm{C}_{9}\mathrm{H}_{10}\mathrm{Br}_{2}$ ) when heated with excess sodamide followed by treatment with dilute HCl gives [Q]. On warming [Q] with mercuric sulphate and dilute sulphuric acid yield $[R]$ which gives positive Iodoform test but negative Tollen's test. The compound $[\mathrm{P}]$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 22nd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Excess $\mathrm{NaNH}{}_{2}$ removes two molecules of HBr from a geminal or vicinal dibromide to give an alkyne; a terminal alkyne is held as its sodium acetylide and is set free by dilute HCl.

$\mathrm{HgSO}{}_{4}$/dil. $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}$ hydrates a terminal alkyne by Markovnikov's rule, so $\mathrm{Ar}-\mathrm{C}\equiv \mathrm{CH}$ gives the methyl ketone $\mathrm{Ar}-\mathrm{CO}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$, which gives a positive iodoform test and, being a ketone, a negative Tollens' test.

In (D), P is the geminal dibromide $p$-$\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{4}-\mathrm{CBr}{}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ ($\mathrm{C}{}_{9}\mathrm{H}{}_{10}\mathrm{Br}{}_{2}$); its $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ group supplies the two hydrogens lost with the two Br atoms:


[IMG]

So Q is 4-ethynyltoluene and R is 4-methylacetophenone.

In (A) the ring-bearing C–Br carbon has no hydrogen, so no $\mathrm{C}\equiv \mathrm{C}$ can form; (B) has its two $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{Br}$ groups on different ring carbons; and (C) is $\mathrm{C}{}_{9}\mathrm{H}{}_{8}\mathrm{Br}{}_{2}$, which does not fit the formula.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

text:
Which of the following mixture gives a buffer solution with $\mathrm{pH}=9.25$ ?

Given : $\mathrm{pK}_{\mathrm{b}}(\mathrm{NH}_{4}\mathrm{OH})=4.75$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 22nd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For a basic buffer of $\mathrm{NH}_{4}\mathrm{OH}$ and its salt $\mathrm{NH}_{4}\mathrm{Cl}$, NCERT uses:

$\mathrm{pOH}=\mathrm{p}K_{b}+\log \left (\frac{[\text{salt}]}{[\text{base}]}\right )$

Given $\mathrm{p}K_{b}(\mathrm{NH}_{4}\mathrm{OH})=4.75$ and required $\mathrm{pH}=9.25$:

$\mathrm{pOH}=14-9.25=4.75$

So,

$4.75=4.75+\log \left (\frac{[\text{salt}]}{[\text{base}]}\right )$

$\Rightarrow \log \left (\frac{[\text{salt}]}{[\text{base}]}\right )=0\Rightarrow \frac{[\text{salt}]}{[\text{base}]}=1$

So, we need equal amounts of salt and base after mixing.

Reaction:

$\mathrm{NH}_{4}\mathrm{OH}+\mathrm{HCl}\to \mathrm{NH}_{4}\mathrm{Cl}+\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$

If initial moles are $n_{b}$ (base) and $n_{a}$ (acid), then after reaction (for buffer, base must be in excess):

moles of salt formed $=n_{a}$

moles of base left $=n_{b}-n_{a}$

Condition for $\dfrac{[\text{salt}]}{[\text{base}]}=1$ is:

$n_{a}=n_{b}-n_{a}\Rightarrow n_{b}=2n_{a}$

Now check options by moles:

Option B
$n_{b}=0.2\times 0.5=0.10\text{mol}$

$n_{a}=0.1\times 0.5=0.05\text{mol}$

Here,

$n_{b}=0.10=2(0.05)=2n_{a}$

So, after reaction:

salt $=0.05$ mol

base left $=0.10-0.05=0.05$ mol  

Equal $\Rightarrow$ required buffer, hence $\mathrm{pOH}=\mathrm{p}K_{b}=4.75$ and $\mathrm{pH}=9.25$.

Correct option: B
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 22nd January Evening Shift

text: When 1 g of compound $(\mathrm{X})$ is subjected to Kjeldahl's method for estimation of nitrogen, 15 mL 1 M $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4}$ was neutralized by ammonia evolved. The percentage of nitrogen in compound $(\mathrm{X})$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 22nd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In Kjeldahl’s method, the ammonia ($\mathrm{NH}_{3}$) evolved neutralizes the acid taken. So,

$\text{equivalents of}\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4}=\text{equivalents of ammonia}$

Given: $15\quad \text{mL}$ of $1~\text{M}\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4}$ is neutralized.

$\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4}$ is a dibasic acid, so $1$ mole of $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4}$ gives $2$ equivalents. Therefore, equivalents of $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4}$ used are:

$\frac{15\times 1\times 2}{1000}$

Ammonia is monobasic (one $\mathrm{NH}_{3}$ neutralizes one equivalent of acid), so:

$\frac{15\times 1\times 2}{1000}=\text{moles of ammonia}\times 1$

So, moles of ammonia $=$ moles of nitrogen ($\mathrm{N}$), because each mole of $\mathrm{NH}_{3}$ contains $1$ mole of $\mathrm{N}$.

Now, mass of nitrogen:

$\text{Weight of nitrogen}=\frac{15\times 1\times 2}{1000}\times 14=0.42$

Percentage of nitrogen in $1~\text{g}$ compound:

$%\text{weight of ’}\mathrm{N}\text{’}=\frac{0.42}{1}\times 100=42%$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 22nd January Evening Shift

text: The energy of first (lowest) Balmer line of H atom is $x\mathrm{J}$. The energy (in J) of second Balmer line of H atom is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 22nd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Balmer lines end at $n=2$. The photon energy for a transition $n\to 2$ in the H atom is

$E=2.18\times 10^{-18}\left (\dfrac{1}{2^{2}}-\dfrac{1}{n^{2}}\right )\text{J}$

First (lowest-energy) Balmer line, $3\to 2$: $E_{1}=2.18\times 10^{-18}\times \left (\dfrac{1}{4}-\dfrac{1}{9}\right )=2.18\times 10^{-18}\times \dfrac{5}{36}\text{J}=x\text{J}$.

Second Balmer line, $4\to 2$: $E_{2}=2.18\times 10^{-18}\times \left (\dfrac{1}{4}-\dfrac{1}{16}\right )=2.18\times 10^{-18}\times \dfrac{3}{16}\text{J}$.

$\dfrac{E_{2}}{E_{1}}=\dfrac{3/16}{5/36}=\dfrac{108}{80}=1.35\Rightarrow E_{2}=1.35x\text{J}$

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 22nd January Evening Shift

text:
Given below are two statements :

Statement I : The first ionization enthalpy of Cr is lower than that of Mn .

Statement II : The second and third ionization enthalpies of Cr are higher than those of Mn . 

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 22nd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Cr is $[\mathrm{Ar}]3d^{5}4s^{1}$ and Mn is $[\mathrm{Ar}]3d^{5}4s^{2}$. Their first, second and third ionisation enthalpies are 653, 1592, 2987 $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ (Cr) and 717, 1509, 3248 $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ (Mn).

First ionisation: Cr loses its single 4s electron to give the stable $3d^{5}$ ion, while Mn has a higher nuclear charge and a filled $4s^{2}$ pair, so $\Delta _{i}H_{1}(\mathrm{Cr})<\Delta _{i}H_{1}(\mathrm{Mn})$. Statement I is true.

Second ionisation: $\mathrm{Cr}{}^{+}$ ($3d^{5}$) must lose an electron from a stable half-filled set, while $\mathrm{Mn}{}^{+}$ ($3d^{5}4s^{1}$) loses its 4s electron to reach $3d^{5}$, so $\Delta _{i}H_{2}(\mathrm{Cr})>\Delta _{i}H_{2}(\mathrm{Mn})$.

Third ionisation: $\mathrm{Mn}{}^{2+}$ ($3d^{5}$) must lose an electron from a stable half-filled set, while $\mathrm{Cr}{}^{2+}$ ($3d^{4}$) has no such stability, so $\Delta _{i}H_{3}(\mathrm{Cr})<\Delta _{i}H_{3}(\mathrm{Mn})$.

Only the second ionisation enthalpy of Cr is higher than that of Mn, so Statement II is false.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 22nd January Evening Shift

text:
At $\mathrm{T}(\mathrm{K}),100\mathrm{g}$ of $98%\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4}(\mathrm{w}/\mathrm{w})$ aqueous solution is mixed with 100 g of $49%\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4}(\mathrm{w}/\mathrm{w})$ aqueous solution. What is the mole fraction of $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4}$ in the resultant solution?

(Given : Atomic mass $\mathrm{H}=1\mathrm{u};\mathrm{S}=32\mathrm{u};\mathrm{O}=16\mathrm{u}$ ).

(Assume that temperature after mixing remains constant)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 22nd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Total mass of $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4}$ in the mixture:

$=\left (100\times \frac{98}{100}\right )+\left (100\times \frac{49}{100}\right )=147\mathrm{gm}$

Here, the first solution gives $98\mathrm{g}$ of $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4}$ and the second gives $49\mathrm{g}$ of $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4}$, so total is $147\mathrm{g}$.

Total mass of solution after mixing $=100+100=200\mathrm{g}$.

So, total mass of $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ in the mixture:

Total weight of $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}=200-147=53\mathrm{gm}$

Moles of $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4}=\frac{147}{98}$ (since molar mass of $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4}$ is $98\mathrm{g}~\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$).

Moles of $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}=\frac{53}{18}$ (since molar mass of $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ is $18\mathrm{g}~\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$).

Now, mole fraction of $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4}$ is:

Mole fraction of $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4}=\frac{\frac{147}{98}}{\left (\frac{147}{98}+\frac{53}{18}\right )}=0.337$

text:
$\text{3, 3-Dimethyl-2-butanol cannot be prepared by :}$


[IMG]

$\text{Choose the correct answer from the options given below :}$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 22nd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
3,3-Dimethyl-2-butanol is $(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{3}\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{OH})-\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$.

In A, $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{MgBr}$ adds a methyl group to the carbonyl carbon of $(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{3}\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{CHO}$, and hydrolysis gives $(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{3}\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{OH})-\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$.

In B, the alkene $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}$ has seven carbon atoms, so its acid-catalysed hydration can only give a heptanol, never the six-carbon target.

In C, ozonolysis of $(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{3}\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3})=\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3})-\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{3}$ gives two molecules of $(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{3}\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{CO}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$, which $\mathrm{NaBH}{}_{4}$ reduces to $(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{3}\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{OH})-\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$.

In D, $\mathrm{LiAlH}{}_{4}$ reduces $(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{3}\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{CO}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ directly to $(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{3}\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{OH})-\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$.

In E, hydration of $(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{3}\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{C}\equiv \mathrm{CH}$ with $\mathrm{Hg}{}^{2+}/\mathrm{H}{}^{+}$ stops at the ketone $(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{3}\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{CO}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$; no reducing agent is present, so no alcohol forms.

Thus only B and E cannot give 3,3-dimethyl-2-butanol.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

text:
$\mathrm{A}+2\mathrm{B}⟶\mathrm{AB}_{2}$

36.0 g of 'A' (Molar mass : $60\mathrm{g}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ ) and 56.0 g of ' B ' (Molar mass : $80\mathrm{g}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ ) are allowed to react. Which of the following statements are correct ?

A. 'A' is the limiting reagent.

B. $77.0\mathrm{g}$ of $\mathrm{AB}_{2}$ is formed.

C. Molar mass of $\mathrm{AB}_{2}$ is $140\mathrm{g}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$.

D. $15.0\mathrm{g}$ of A is left unreacted after the completion of reaction.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 22nd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Moles taken: $n_{\text{A}}=\dfrac{36.0}{60}=0.60$ mol and $n_{\text{B}}=\dfrac{56.0}{80}=0.70$ mol.

From $\mathrm{A}+\qquad 2\mathrm{B}\longrightarrow \mathrm{AB}{}_{2}$, $0.60$ mol of A needs $1.20$ mol of B, but only $0.70$ mol of B is present, so B is the limiting reagent and statement A is false.

$0.70$ mol of B forms $\dfrac{0.70}{2}=0.35$ mol of $\mathrm{AB}{}_{2}$. Molar mass of $\mathrm{AB}{}_{2}=60+2(80)=220\text{g mol}^{-1}$, so statement C is false.

Mass of $\mathrm{AB}{}_{2}$ formed $=0.35\times 220=77.0$ g, so statement B is true.

A consumed $=0.35$ mol $=0.35\times 60=21.0$ g, so A left unreacted $=36.0-21.0=15.0$ g and statement D is true.

Only statements B and D are correct.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 22nd January Evening Shift

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 22nd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The compound is an ester, $\mathrm{R}-\mathrm{COO}-\mathrm{R}{}^{'}$, named as "alkyl alkanoate" with the group on oxygen cited first.

The group on oxygen is $-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$, that is propyl ($n$-propyl).

In the acyl part the carbonyl carbon is C-1. The longest chain from C-1 runs through C-2 (bearing $\mathrm{Br}$), C-3, C-4, C-5 and then along the two-carbon branch (C-6, C-7), giving seven carbons: heptanoate. The remaining one-carbon branch is a methyl group on C-5.


[IMG]

The acyl part is therefore 2-bromo-5-methylheptanoate, and the ester is propyl 2-bromo-5-methylheptanoate ($n$-propyl 2-bromo-5-methylheptanoate).

Hence, the correct option is (C).

text:
Consider the following electrochemical cell :

$\mathrm{Pt}|\mathrm{O}_{2}(\mathrm{g})(1\mathrm{bar})|\mathrm{HCl}(\mathrm{aq})\|\mathrm{M}^{2+}(\mathrm{aq},1.0\mathrm{M})|\mathrm{M}(\mathrm{s})$

The pH above which, oxygen gas would start to evolve at anode is $____$ (nearest integer).

$\left. \left [\begin{array}{ll} \text{Given :} & \mathrm{E}\mathrm{o}\mathrm{M}2+/\mathrm{M}=0.994\mathrm{V} \\  & \mathrm{E}\mathrm{o}\mathrm{O}2/\mathrm{H}2\mathrm{O}=1.23\mathrm{V} \end{array}\right \}\text{standard reduction potential}\text{and}\mathrm{RT}\mathrm{F}(2.303)=0.059\mathrm{V}\text{at the given condition}\right ]$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 22nd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For the oxygen electrode (reduction reaction):

$\mathrm{O}_{2}(\mathrm{g})+4\mathrm{H}^{+}(\mathrm{aq})+4e^{-}\to 2\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{l})$

Nernst equation:

$E_{\mathrm{O}_{2}/\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}}=E_{\mathrm{O}_{2}/\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}}^{\circ }-\frac{0.059}{4}\log \left (\frac{1}{p_{\mathrm{O}2}[\mathrm{H}^{+}]^{4}}\right )$

Given $p_{\mathrm{O}_{2}}=1$ bar, so $\log p_{\mathrm{O}_{2}}=0$:

$E_{\mathrm{O}_{2}/\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}}=1.23+0.059\log [\mathrm{H}^{+}]$

Since $\log [\mathrm{H}^{+}]=-\mathrm{pH}$:

$E_{\mathrm{O}_{2}/\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}}=1.23-0.059\mathrm{pH}$

For the metal electrode:

$\mathrm{M}^{2+}+2e^{-}\to \mathrm{M}(\mathrm{s})$

Given $[\mathrm{M}^{2+}]=1.0\mathrm{M}$, hence

$E_{\mathrm{M}^{2+}/\mathrm{M}}=E_{\mathrm{M}^{2+}/\mathrm{M}}^{\circ }=0.994\mathrm{V}$

Oxygen will start evolving at the anode when the oxygen electrode becomes the anode, i.e. when its reduction potential becomes less than that of $\mathrm{M}^{2+}/\mathrm{M}$. The threshold is when both are equal:

$1.23-0.059\mathrm{pH}=0.994$

$0.059\mathrm{pH}=1.23-0.994=0.236$

$\mathrm{pH}=\frac{0.236}{0.059}=4$

So, oxygen gas starts evolving at the anode for $\mathrm{pH}>4$.

$4$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 22nd January Evening Shift

text:
The mass of benzanilide obtained from the benzoylation reaction of 5.8 g of aniline, if yield of product is $82%$, is $____$ g (nearest integer).

(Given molar mass in $\mathrm{g}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}\mathrm{H}:1,\mathrm{C}:12,\mathrm{N}:14,\mathrm{O}:16$ )
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 22nd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Benzoylation of aniline with benzoyl chloride gives benzanilide in a 1 : 1 mole ratio:

$\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{NH}{}_{2}+\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{COCl}\longrightarrow \mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{NHCOC}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}+\mathrm{HCl}$

Molar mass of aniline, $\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{7}\mathrm{N}=6(12)+7(1)+14=93\text{g mol}^{-1}$, so $n=\dfrac{5.8}{93}=0.0624\text{mol}$.

Molar mass of benzanilide, $\mathrm{C}{}_{13}\mathrm{H}{}_{11}\mathrm{NO}=13(12)+11(1)+14+16=197\text{g mol}^{-1}$.

At 82% yield, moles of benzanilide $=0.0624\times 0.82=0.0511\text{mol}$, and its mass $=0.0511\times 197=10.06\text{g}\approx 10\text{g}$.

Hence, the answer is 10.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 22nd January Evening Shift

text:
Among the following oxides of $3d$ elements, the number of mixed oxides are $____$ .

$\mathrm{Ti}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3},\mathrm{V}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{4},\mathrm{Cr}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3},\mathrm{Mn}_{3}\mathrm{O}_{4},\mathrm{Fe}_{3}\mathrm{O}_{4},\mathrm{Fe}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3},\mathrm{Co}_{3}\mathrm{O}_{4}$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 22nd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Mixed oxides are those oxides which can be written as a combination of two simpler oxides of the same metal, like $MO\cdot M_{2}O_{3}$.

Now, check the given oxides and see which ones can be written in this form:

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{Mn}_{3}\mathrm{O}_{4}=\mathrm{MnO}\cdot \mathrm{Mn}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3} \\ \mathrm{Fe}_{3}\mathrm{O}_{4}=\mathrm{FeO}\cdot \mathrm{Fe}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3} \\ \mathrm{Co}_{3}\mathrm{O}_{4}=\mathrm{CoO}\cdot \mathrm{Co}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3} \end{array}\begin{array}{l} \text{Only three} \\ \text{mixed oxides} \end{array}$

So, the number of mixed oxides in the given list is $3$.

text:
Consider $\mathrm{A}\leftarrow ^{\mathrm{k}_{1}}\mathrm{B}$ and $\mathrm{C}\leftarrow ^{\mathrm{k}_{2}}\mathrm{D}$ are two reactions. If the rate constant $(\mathrm{k}_{1})$ of the $\mathrm{A}⟶\mathrm{B}$ reaction can be expressed by the following equation $\log _{10}\mathrm{k}=14.34-\frac{1.5\times 10^{4}}{\mathrm{T}/\mathrm{K}}$ and activation energy of $C⟶D$ reaction $(Ea_{2})$ is $\frac{1}{5}$ th of the $A⟶B$ reaction $(Ea_{1})$, then the value of $(Ea_{2})$ is

$____$ $\mathrm{kJ}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$. (Nearest Integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 22nd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given: $\log _{10}\mathrm{k}=14.34-\frac{1.5\times 10^{4}}{\mathrm{T}/\mathrm{K}}$

From the Arrhenius equation in base-10 form, we write:

$\log _{10}k=\log _{10}A-\frac{E_{a}}{2.303RT}$

On comparing this with $\log _{10}\mathrm{k}=14.34-\frac{1.5\times 10^{4}}{\mathrm{T}/\mathrm{K}}$, the coefficient of $\frac{1}{T}$ gives:

$\frac{\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{a}1}}{2.303\mathrm{R}}=1.5\times 10^{4}$

Now substitute $\mathrm{R}=8.314\mathrm{J}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}\mathrm{K}^{-1}$:

$\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{a}_{1}}=1.5\times 10^{4}\times 2.303\times 8.314$

$\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{a}_{1}}=28.7207\times 10^{4}\mathrm{J}$

Convert joules to kilojoules ($1\mathrm{kJ}=10^{3}\mathrm{J}$):

$\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{a}_{1}}=287.207\mathrm{kJ}$

Given $\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{a}_{2}}=\frac{1}{5}\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{a}_{1}}$, so:

$\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{a}_{2}}=\frac{\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{a}1}}{5}=\frac{287.207}{5}=57.44\mathrm{kJ}$
